function_revised: Small integral membrane protein (DUF2530) under strong purifying selection; its fold resembles actinobacterial respiratory-supercomplex accessory membrane subunits (HHpred 7Q21 Cgl2017 ~92% E0.24). CAVEAT: fold resemblance ONLY, no genomic/co-expression/structural corroboration that it is a subunit; not part of a validated functional module.
evidence: HHpred: top 3 hits are actinobacterial/mycobacterial respiratory-supercomplex membrane proteins (7Q21_h Corynebacterium supercomplex 92.5% E0.24; 9QEF Actinobacteria supercomplex 90%; 9GY6 mycobacterial cytochrome-bc TM 87% E1.5), plus PRSAF1 7E1V 65% and Rieske 7E1V_M 56%; these sit above the generic TM-helix-promiscuity floor (MerF/CD4/Mg-transporters <79%). Borderline E-values + TM noise -> low. DUF2530, strong purifying. Same cluster as Rv0615/Rv1892/Rv2843/Rv0344c.

HHpred web (MPI Bioinformatics Toolkit, profile-profile remote homology), interpreted in project 'Still unknown gene function', 2026-06-10. A fold/family-level assignment, not a demonstrated function.

Case-study refutation (2026-06-12): the 5 small dark membrane/lipoproteins originally flagged as supercomplex subunits are dispersed (0.4-3.2 Mb), none near qcrCAB(Rv2194-6)/ctaCDE, STRING anchors are genomic neighbours (regulators/methyltransferases) NOT respiratory genes, and no literature/structure models them as subunits -> fold resemblance only, NOT a validated functional module.
